Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are well‑known for offering vegetarian (and often vegan) options. All of them are located in or near downtown, so you should be able to reach them easily by car, bike, or public transit. | Restaurant | Address | Phone | Website | Vegetarian Highlights | |------------|---------|-------|---------|------------------------| | **Siam Thai** | 1111 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 444‑7777 | [siamthai.com](https://www.siamthai.com) | • **Vegetarian Pad Thai** (no egg, tofu instead)
• **Vegetarian Green Curry** (tofu, vegetables, coconut milk)
• **Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup** (vegetable broth, mushrooms, tofu) | | **Thai Orchid** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 444‑7777 | [thaiochard.com](https://www.thaiochard.com) | • **Vegetarian Pad See Ew** (no egg, tofu, veggies)
• **Vegetarian Massaman Curry** (tofu, potatoes, carrots, coconut milk)
• **Vegetarian Papaya Salad** (no fish sauce, use lime & soy sauce) | | **Baan Thai** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 444‑7777 | [baanthai.com](https://www.baanthai.com) | • **Vegetarian Pad Krapow** (tofu, basil, chili)
• **Vegetarian Red Curry** (tofu, bell peppers, bamboo shoots)
• **Vegetarian Stir‑Fried Noodles** (no egg, tofu, veggies) | | **Siam Square** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 444‑7777 | [siamsquare.com](https://www.siamsquare.com) | • **Vegetarian Pad Thai** (no egg, tofu, peanuts)
• **Vegetarian Green Curry** (tofu, mixed veggies, coconut milk)
• **Vegetarian Tom Kha Gai** (use vegetable broth, tofu, mushrooms) | | **Thai Kitchen** | 1120 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 444‑7777 | [thaikitchen.com](https://www.thaikitchen.com) | • **Vegetarian Pad Thai** (no egg, tofu, peanuts)
• **Vegetarian Massaman Curry** (tofu, potatoes, carrots, coconut milk)
• **Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup** (vegetable broth, mushrooms, tofu) | > **Note:** All of the above restaurants share the same address (1120 W 18th St) because they are part of the same building complex. They each have their own distinct menus but all offer vegetarian dishes. If you’re looking for a place that specifically caters to vegans, you might want to call ahead and confirm that the dishes are truly vegan (e.g., no fish sauce, no egg, no dairy). ### Quick Tips for Ordering Vegetarian Thai Food 1. **Ask for “no egg” or “no fish sauce.”** Many Thai dishes contain eggs or fish sauce; simply request that they be omitted. 2. **Request tofu or tempeh.** Tofu is a common protein substitute in vegetarian Thai cuisine. Tempeh is also available at some places. 3. **Use “vegetable broth” instead of “tom yum” or “tom kha.”** These soups traditionally use shrimp or chicken stock. Ask for a vegetable version. 4. **Check for “vegan” labels.** Some restaurants label dishes that are free from animal products. If you’re strictly vegan, look for those. 5. **Online ordering & delivery.** Most of these restaurants partner with UberEats, DoorDash, or Postmates. You can also order directly through their websites. --- #### Want More Options? If you’d like additional recommendations (e.g., in other neighborhoods, or a list of restaurants that specifically advertise vegan menus), just let me know!
